correctness.rationale: Generic simplex j-faces in a section correspond bijectively to crossed (j+1)-faces, giving binomial difference f_j=C(N,j+2)-C(K,j+2)-C(N-K,j+2); normal coordinates are centered independent Gaussians, and the vertex-directed displacement gives the shared threshold G_i-Gbar>h_n(G_0-Gbar). A uniform local empirical-cdf increment bound gives the critical influence variable (1/sqrt(n)) sum(1_{G_i>0}-1/2-φ(0)G_i)-cφ(0)G_0 with variance 1/4+(c²-1)/(2π), then symmetric binomial Taylor expansion yields rank-one scaled chi-square deficits. Uniform Glivenko–Cantelli and Taylor expansion give the mesoscopic n²h_n² normalization, and strong cdf convergence gives macroscopic p=Φ(hZ) and all bounded fixed-rank moments. The exact expected-vertex formula follows from bivariate Gaussian sign correlations; endpoint h=1 is only a limit of finite h<1. The proof uses stochastic equicontinuity for dependent moving threshold via deterministic-grid control, not simulated limiting distributions.
